seo.defaultTitle: Interactive Kabbalah — Kabbalah, tarot and alchemy as maps
seo.defaultDescription: Explore the Tree of Life, Rider-Waite Tarot and alchemy in interactive maps. Tap any symbol to uncover its meaning. Free, no sign-up required.
seo.keywords: kabbalah, tree of life, sephirot, rider-waite tarot, alchemy, alchemical symbols

tree.title: Interactive Tree of Life
tree.description: Ten Sephirot, 22 paths and the Qliphoth on a single map. Tap any sphere for divine names, correspondences and the text of each path.
tree.keywords: tree of life, kabbalah, sephirot, qliphoth, 22 paths, kabbalistic correspondences

tarot.title: Interactive Rider-Waite Tarot
tarot.description: The 22 major arcana, card by card, with Pamela Colman Smith's art and readings symbol by symbol.
tarot.keywords: tarot, rider-waite, major arcana, interactive tarot, pamela colman smith

alchemicalSymbols.title: Alchemical Symbols
alchemicalSymbols.description: Elements, planets and the processes of the Great Work in a visual catalogue, with the meaning of each sign and its place in the work.
alchemicalSymbols.keywords: alchemy, alchemical symbols, great work, elements, planets

card.description: Major arcana {roman} of the Rider-Waite tarot — the art, the symbols and the correspondences of {name}.
card.title: {name} — Major Arcana {roman}

minorCard.title: {name} — Minor Arcana
minorCard.description: {name}, a card of the suit of {suit} in the Rider-Waite Tarot: artwork, symbols and Kabbalistic correspondences.

tarot.hint: Hover (or tap) the symbols on the card to reveal their meaning. Click to pin.
tarot.panelEmptyHint: Hover or tap a symbol on the card to see its meaning here.

theHighPriestess.name: The High Priestess
theHighPriestess.intro: Guardian of the sanctuary behind the veil, the High Priestess is the silent memory between the two pillars of the Temple. Explore each symbol of the card.

pillarB.title: The Pillar B (Boaz)
pillarB.description: The black pillar of Boaz represents severity, contraction and form. It is the principle that delimits and gives structure, without which no manifestation can exist.

pillarJ.title: The Pillar J (Jachin)
pillarJ.description: The white pillar of Jachin represents mercy, expansion and force. It is the principle that gives and expands, making room for life to flourish.

veilPomegranates.title: The Veil with Pomegranates
veilPomegranates.description: The veil embroidered with pomegranates and palms hides the sanctum: knowledge reveals itself only to those who pass through — not to those who peep. The pomegranates evoke Persephone and the underworlds.

water.title: The Sea Behind the Veil
water.description: Between the pillars, beyond the veil, stretches the ocean: the collective unconscious, the matrix of every form not yet manifested.

scroll.title: The TORA Scroll
scroll.description: Partly hidden in her lap, the scroll of the Law rests: wisdom exists, but remains veiled — intuition before letter.

crown.title: The Lunar Crown
crown.description: The crescent horns embrace the solar disc: the High Priestess unites Moon and Sun, reception and radiation, in the same gesture of Hathor.

solarCross.title: The Solar Cross on Her Chest
solarCross.description: The equal-armed cross over her heart: the axis of balance between opposites, the still point of the center.

crescentMoon.title: The Moon at Her Feet
crescentMoon.description: The lunar crescent beneath her robes: everything here is governed by the Moon — cycles, tides, the unconscious and the deep feminine.

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.intro: The angel of alchemy balances the waters of the soul between two cups, uniting opposites on the middle path. Explore each symbol of the card.

crownHalo.title: Solar Crown / Halo
crownHalo.description: The solar disc on the brow and the radiant halo mark illumination and the divine presence. Temperance acts guided by the light of higher consciousness.

wings.title: Wings
wings.description: The great wings reveal the angelic nature and the ability to move between heaven and earth, spirit and matter.

triangleSquare.title: Triangle in the Square
triangleSquare.description: The triangle (fire, spirit) inscribed in the square (matter, the four elements) symbolizes spirit manifested and contained within form — balance between the divine and the material.

cupsWater.title: The Cups and the Water
cupsWater.description: Water flowing between the two cups, often on an impossible diagonal, represents the alchemical fusion of opposites: conscious and unconscious, past and future. The essence of temperance — mixing in the right measure.

sunMountain.title: Sun, Mountains and the Path
sunMountain.description: In the background, the rising sun over the mountains and the winding path point to the journey toward spiritual realization — the distant golden crown as the goal.

irises.title: Irises
irises.description: The yellow irises allude to Iris, messenger of the gods and goddess of the rainbow, linking the divine and human worlds. They reinforce communication and harmony.

waterFeet.title: The Water at the Feet
waterFeet.description: One foot submerged in water (the unconscious, emotion) and the other firm on land (the conscious, the material) show the perfect balance between the two worlds.

theFool.name: The Fool
theFool.intro: On the edge of the abyss, the eternal beginner sets out with no visible baggage — only faith, instinct and the light that guides him. Explore each symbol of the card.

sun.title: The Radiant Sun
sun.description: The sun shines behind the Fool's shoulder: the divine blessing that accompanies whoever dares the leap. Its light is the inner certainty that needs no planning.

mountains.title: The Snowy Mountains
mountains.description: The snow-capped peaks in the distance are the heights of spiritual aspiration — the far-off goal the traveler does not even need to face yet; it is enough to walk.

cliff.title: The Cliff
cliff.description: The abyss at the edge of the step is the unknown. The Fool does not notice it — or does not mind: faith does not calculate, it trusts. This is the zero point of every journey.

bundle.title: The Bundle on the Staff
bundle.description: The colorful bundle hanging from the staff carries the archetypes of the collective unconscious — the heritage every traveler carries without knowing what it holds.

whiteRose.title: The White Rose
whiteRose.description: In his left hand, the white rose is the purity of intention and the untouched innocence: the unblemished principle of every beginning.

motleyTunic.title: The Motley Tunic
motleyTunic.description: The Fool's patchwork coat of many colors is a harlequin's garment: every patch is a life, a mask, a role he has tried on without clinging to any of them. The tunic reminds us that the world is play and festival — whoever wears every color need not pick a single identity before setting out.

mismatchedLeggings.title: The Mismatched Legs
mismatchedLeggings.description: The Fool's two legs do not match: one color on each side, one stride longer than the other. This asymmetry is the signature of one who walks before being ready — the crooked step keeps the motion going, and it is the imbalance that pushes him into the unknown. It is not carelessness: it is courage in transit.

jesterCap.title: The Fool's Cap
jesterCap.description: The court jester's cap is the Fool's only crown: to reign without a throne, over nothing, starting from zero. The ridiculous hat is wisdom in disguise — whoever accepts being a fool before the world is free to learn everything anew.

dog.title: The Little White Dog
dog.description: The dog leaping at the Fool's feet is faithful instinct — and also a warning: the loyalty of the animal body accompanies, barks and protects, but does not decide the leap.

feather.title: The Red Feather
feather.description: The red feather on his cap recalls the lightness required: vibrant courage, without the weight of certainties.

theMagician.name: The Magician
theMagician.intro: As above, so below: the Magician is the channel between heaven and earth, with every tool of creation within reach. Explore each symbol of the card.

infinity.title: The Infinity Symbol
infinity.description: The vertical lemniscate above his head is the key to the arcana: an unlimited mind, complete command of the vocabulary of creation.

wand.title: The Raised Wand
wand.description: The wand raised in his right hand draws down divine force; the Magician does not own it, he only conducts it.

pointingHand.title: The Hand Pointing Down
pointingHand.description: His free hand points to the earth: the hermetic principle 'as above, so below' — every inspiration must become flesh in matter.

tableTools.title: The Table and the Four Suits
tableTools.description: On the table lie cup, sword, wand and pentacle: the four elements — emotion, mind, will and body — the tools of manifestation.

roseGarden.title: The Rose Garden
roseGarden.description: Roses and lilies bloom before the table: desire and purity cultivated side by side — matter already transmuted into paradise.

serpentBelt.title: The Serpent Belt
serpentBelt.description: The serpent biting its own tail (ouroboros) at his waist: eternity and self-renewal — power held within a closed circle.

theEmpress.name: The Empress
theEmpress.intro: Sovereign of fertile nature, the Empress reigns over wheat, waters and all that blooms. Explore each symbol of the card.

starCrown.title: The Crown of Twelve Stars
starCrown.description: Twelve stars: the complete zodiac — she governs the cyclical time of seasons and gestations.

venusShield.title: The Shield of Venus
venusShield.description: The heart-shaped shield bearing the symbol of Venus: love as foundation — beauty, affection and vital magnetism.

scepter.title: The Scepter
scepter.description: The globe-topped scepter: gentle authority over the world of forms — her hand does not even need to grip it tightly.

wheatField.title: The Wheat Field
wheatField.description: The ripe wheat at the foot of the throne: Demeter and the abundance of the Mother — work that bears fruit without haste.

pomegranateRobe.title: The Pomegranates of Her Robe
pomegranateRobe.description: The dress patterned with pomegranates (echoing the High Priestess's veil): fertility, many children, many seeds — the multiplication of the one.

riverTrees.title: The River and the Trees
riverTrees.description: In the background, the waterfall and the forest: life flowing without a dam — nature renewing itself within its own rhythm.

theEmperor.name: The Emperor
theEmperor.intro: The archetype of the Father: structure, law and iron will enthroned upon power.

ramHeads.title: The Rams of the Throne
ramHeads.description: The rams' heads carved into the arms of the throne: Aries and Mars — the initiating force, the impulse that opens every new cycle.

ankh.title: The Ankh Scepter
ankh.description: The ankh cross is the life the Emperor grants and sustains: his power exists to organize and preserve existence, not to destroy it.

orb.title: The Orb
orb.description: In his left hand, the globe of dominion: the world under conscious control — complete vision, government from afar.

armor.title: The Armor Beneath the Mantle
armor.description: Under the red robes, the breastplate: the ruler remains a warrior within even when serene without — the rigidity that protects and also imprisons.

beardCrown.title: The Beard and the Crown
beardCrown.description: The long white beard is the wisdom accumulated by time; the golden crown, the right to command inherited from experience — not from whim.

mountains.title: The Arid Mountains
mountains.description: The rocky desert in the background: the realm of form in its driest, most defined state — clear limits, without dissolution.

theHierophant.name: The Hierophant
theHierophant.intro: The priest of tradition: between the temple columns, he blesses and keeps the keys of the established mystery.

tripleCrown.title: The Triple Crown
tripleCrown.description: The three bands of the tiara: the three worlds — physical, mental and spiritual — under a single authority; pope, emperor and god in one office.

tripleCross.title: The Triple Cross
tripleCross.description: The staff with three crossbars: blessing descends through every level of existence, from heaven to earth.

crossedKeys.title: The Crossed Keys
crossedKeys.description: Of gold and silver, sun and moon: the keys that open the outer and inner mysteries — the exoteric and the esoteric set in a cross.

blessingHand.title: The Hand in Blessing
blessingHand.description: The two raised fingers: the gesture of teaching and blessing — doctrine handed down from hand to hand, from generation to generation.

acolytes.title: The Two Monks
acolytes.description: The tonsured initiates in embroidered cloaks — obedience and devotion: tradition exists only because there are those who receive it.

pillars.title: The Temple Pillars
pillars.description: Unlike those of the High Priestess (J and B), these belong to the established: the visible church, the structure that sustains the sacred in matter.

theChariot.name: The Chariot
theChariot.intro: A serene victor of battles past, the charioteer drives opposing sphinxes without reins — by will alone.

starryCanopy.title: The Starry Canopy
starryCanopy.description: The woven sky that roofs the chariot: celestial protection and destinies — the stars that accompany those who move with purpose.

sphinxes.title: The White and Black Sphinxes
sphinxes.description: The opposing forces the charioteer does not tame by force but orchestrates by direction: without reins, intention governs.

wingedSun.title: The Winged Solar Disc
wingedSun.description: The Egyptian emblem at the front of the chariot: the uplifted heart — the victory of one who has mastered himself before conquering the world.

shoulderMoons.title: The Moons on His Shoulders
shoulderMoons.description: The crescents on his shoulder plates: intuition and receptivity traveling alongside determination — the lunar in the service of the solar.

cityWalls.title: The City Behind
cityWalls.description: The walls are left behind: what has been conquered already lies at the rear; the Chariot advances through open ground — new challenges, without walls.

squareEmblem.title: The Square on His Chest
squareEmblem.description: The square symbol on his breastplate: the squared will — four elements, four directions — geometric firmness at the center of action.

strength.name: Strength
strength.intro: Not the strength that subjugates, but the one that tames by gentleness — roses where there would be chains.

infinity.title: The Infinity Above Her Head
infinity.description: The same lemniscate worn by the Magician, now on the woman's brow: spiritual strength — the power that comes from above, not from muscle.

lionMouth.title: The Lion's Mouth
lionMouth.description: Her fingers intertwined with the lion's jaws: raw instinct is not beaten down but embraced — the animal ego tamed by affectionate firmness.

roseGarland.title: The Garland of Roses
roseGarland.description: Roses crown her head and waist: the bonds here are bonds of beauty — desire (red) transformed into conscious adornment.

redRibbon.title: The Red Ribbon
redRibbon.description: The red sash at her waist: appetite is not eliminated in the taming — only tied in a graceful bow.

whiteRobe.title: The White Robe
whiteRobe.description: The simple tunic: purity of intention — nothing to defend, no armor; courage unarmed.

mountains.title: The Mountains Behind
mountains.description: The horizon of peaks in the background: the task is long — taming the lion is daily practice, not a single event.

theHermit.name: The Hermit
theHermit.intro: On the snowy peak of attainment, the sage looks within: the light he carries is the one he finds.

lanternStar.title: The Lantern and the Seal of Solomon
lanternStar.description: Raised to eye level, the lantern displays the hexagram: the wisdom sought outside shines here within — to seek is to remember.

staff.title: The Staff
staff.description: The pilgrim's staff is the column that sustains the solitary walk — and the humble scepter of one who already reigns over himself.

grayHood.title: The Gray Hood
grayHood.description: The faded cloak, without a crest: the anonymity of the true master — knowledge is not displayed, it is kindled in others.

mountainPeak.title: The Mountain Peak
mountainPeak.description: He stands on the summit that every previous arcana climbed: from such a height, what was urgent looks small — and still he keeps searching.

beardedFace.title: The Face of the Sage
beardedFace.description: The white beard and the lowered gaze: an age that does not weigh — time distilled into understanding, silence as his mother tongue.

theLovers.name: The Lovers
theLovers.intro: Under Raphael's blessing, the soul chooses: the flaming tree and the serpent's tree, the man and the woman, desire and consciousness.

angel.title: The Angel Raphael
angel.description: With wings spread, Raphael — "God heals" — presides over the union: love as a regenerative force and a conscious choice, not blind yearning.

sun.title: The Sun
sun.description: The golden disc behind the angel: the truth that illuminates every authentic union — nothing to hide beneath the full light.

flamingTree.title: The Flaming Tree
flamingTree.description: Behind the man, the blazing tree is the zeal of the will: the yang fire, the passion that illuminates and devours.

serpentTree.title: The Tree of the Serpent
serpentTree.description: Behind the woman, the tree of knowledge with the serpent coiled around it: received wisdom, yin magnetism — the desire that seduces into experience.

couple.title: The Man and the Woman
couple.description: He looks at her; she looks at the angel: consciousness turned toward the unconscious, the unconscious turned toward spirit — the triangle of every transforming relationship.

mountain.title: The Mountain
mountain.description: The distant peak between the two: union as ascent — the sublime goal reached by two, never alone.

wheelOfFortune.name: Wheel of Fortune
wheelOfFortune.intro: The still axis of eternal return: Anubis rises, Typhon descends — and the Sphinx waits at the top with the answer.

angel.title: The Angel — Matthew
angel.description: In the upper left corner, the angel reads its book: the Man of Aquarius, the fixed air of intelligence. In Matthew, the genealogy that joins heaven and earth — the consciousness that contemplates the turning and recognizes the divine hand within it.

eagle.title: The Eagle — John
eagle.description: At the upper right, the eagle perches on the book: Scorpio, fixed water, the eye that sees the invisible. In John, the Word that was in the beginning — the vision that passes through death and rises above the turning itself.

bull.title: The Ox — Luke
bull.description: At the lower left, the ox rests with its book open: Taurus, fixed earth, the gentle strength that sustains. In Luke, sacrifice and labor — the fertile matter where the wheel finds ground to turn.

lion.title: The Lion — Mark
lion.description: At the lower right, the lion guards the book: Leo, fixed fire, the heart that roars. In Mark, courage and the Kingdom — the fire that drives the turning and refuses to be extinguished.

wheelLetters.title: The Letters of the Wheel
wheelLetters.description: TARO (or ROTA, TORAT) interwoven with the Hebrew letters Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh: the Law that turns — the divine Name that becomes world, the world that, turned, becomes Name again.

alchemicalRim.title: The Alchemical Rim
alchemicalRim.description: Sulfur, mercury, water and salt in the outer quadrants: the wheel is the workshop of the Great Work itself — continuous transmutation.

sphinx.title: The Sphinx at the Top
sphinx.description: Motionless at the highest point, sword raised: the riddle and the balance — the only creature that neither rises nor falls, because it is already the axis.

anubis.title: Anubis Ascending
anubis.description: The Egyptian psychopomp climbs with the wheel: evolution — the soul rising turn by turn, guided by what it learned to honor.

serpentTyphon.title: The Serpent Typhon
serpentTyphon.description: Descending in a spiral: involution, the drag of matter — every ascent has its counterweight going down.

justice.name: Justice
justice.intro: Between the pillars of the law, the sword and the scales: every act weighed with the same stone.

pillarsVeil.title: The Pillars and the Veil
pillarsVeil.description: Behind her, pillars and a veil: Justice acts within structure — the verdict is human, but the court is cosmic.

scales.title: The Scales
scales.description: In her left hand, the beam balanced at zero: exact equilibrium between what was done and what is owed — the mathematics of karma, without pity and without cruelty.

sword.title: The Upright Sword
sword.description: In her right hand, with an impeccable edge: the truth that cuts — to decide is to separate, and judging demands a blade clean of vanity.

crown.title: The Crown
crown.description: The three-tiered crown: thought, word and deed under the same measure — the law that reigns before it punishes.

redMantle.title: The Red Mantle
redMantle.description: Beneath the pale tunic, the red mantle: passion exists, but underlying — the judge feels, and for that very reason weighs with both hands.

theHangedMan.name: The Hanged Man
theHangedMan.intro: Suspended between heaven and earth by the ankle, the voluntary mystic: a surrender that is not defeat.

beam.title: The Tau Beam
beam.description: The gallows shaped like a T — the Tau, sign of salvation: the same cross that punishes is the one that redeems, depending on which side one hangs from.

livingTree.title: The Living Tree
livingTree.description: Green leaves sprout from the timber: the sacrifice is made on a living tree, not on dead wood — every surrender here bears fruit.

halo.title: The Golden Halo
halo.description: Around the inverted head: light is not lost through sacrifice — it intensifies. Illumination through surrender.

crossedLeg.title: The Crossed Leg
crossedLeg.description: The legs trace the numeral 4 — the world of form — and the whole body an inverted cross: matter hung on the spirit's turned perspective, the world read upside down.

boundHands.title: The Hands Bound Behind the Back
boundHands.description: Tied behind the trunk in a triangle: the will that gives itself over — hands that do not grasp allow the heights to fill them.

sereneFace.title: The Serene Face
sereneFace.description: No anguish on the face: the surrender is complete and conscious — whoever chose to hang is not the rope's victim, but its dance partner.

death.name: Death
death.intro: Not the end but the passage: the sun rises between two towers while every hierarchy kneels.

risingSun.title: The Sun Between the Towers
risingSun.description: Between two towers the sun rises — and does not set: the hidden promise of arcanum XIII. Every crossing ends in dawn.

riverBoat.title: The River and the Boat
riverBoat.description: The boat waits on the river: the crossing every soul must make — the ferryman of old now waits; the river never stops flowing, only we stop.

skeletonArmor.title: The Skeleton in Armor
skeletonArmor.description: Bones beneath black armor: what remains when every form falls — the final structure, the invincible that is already bone and therefore fears nothing.

blackHorse.title: The White Horse
blackHorse.description: The "pale" steed of scripture, whiter than any other creature in the arcanum: death rides over the pure — nothing impure reaches the other shore.

bannerRose.title: The Banner of the White Rose
bannerRose.description: The five-petalled rose on the black cloth: life persisting within the symbol of death — transformation, not annihilation; the five senses surrendering.

kneelingFigures.title: Those Who Kneel
kneelingFigures.description: King, woman and child: power, attachment and innocence — the three human reactions before the inevitable: resistance, grief and acceptance.

childFlowers.title: The Child and the Flowers
childFlowers.description: Only the child raises flowers to the rider: innocence welcomes transformation as springtime — death seen by fearless eyes is metamorphosis.

theTower.name: The Tower
theTower.intro: The lightning bolt that strikes down the false crown: no one falls from the Tower by chance — each falls from himself.

towerCrag.title: The Tower on the Crag
towerCrag.description: Upon the bare rock, with no foundations in sight: the structure believed eternal — built on what was unseen, it falls when the unseen shifts.

lightning.title: The Lightning
lightning.description: It descends exactly through the crown of the tower: sudden intervention — truth that asks no leave and strikes first what stood highest, because it rested on the falsest ground.

fallingCrown.title: The Falling Crown
fallingCrown.description: Torn from the top of the tower, still in its fall: every power founded on error adorns itself with what it cannot sustain — authority collapsing along with the structure.

fallingFigures.title: The Two Who Fall
fallingFigures.description: Head over heels, like the Hanged Man — but without halo and without choice: here surrender was not voluntary; awakening arrived as an earthquake.

flamesYods.title: The Yods of Fire
flamesYods.description: Twenty-two tongues of fire shaped like the Hebrew letter Yod: the divine seed scattered through the ruin — the same fire that topples the Tower sows the alphabet of rebuilding (22 letters, 22 paths).

theStar.name: The Star
theStar.intro: After the storm the sky opens: the Giver pours her waters over the earth and over the lake.

greatStar.title: The Great Star
greatStar.description: The larger star with eight rays: hope that does not depend on circumstance — Venus, the morning star, announcing the Sun without being the Sun.

sevenStars.title: The Seven Smaller Stars
sevenStars.description: Seven little suns around her: the seven chakras, the seven classical planets — the intermediate hierarchy between you and the Great Star.

twoJugs.title: The Two Jugs
twoJugs.description: Water poured in two directions — onto the land (the body, the practical) and into the lake (the soul, the unconscious): feeding both worlds from the same source.

ibis.title: The Ibis in the Tree
ibis.description: The bird of Thoth at the water's edge: thought renewing itself — after the purification of the Tower, the first bird to return is serene reflection.

pool.title: The Pool
pool.description: The still water that receives: the unconscious replenished — the psyche that does not ask to understand, only to be bathed.

horizon.title: The Earth and the Horizon
horizon.description: The ground and the limit of the sky: the promise of integration — what descended from above will grow in the soil; hope that becomes a plant.

theMoon.name: The Moon
theMoon.intro: On the path between two towers, what rises from the lake has no name yet: dog, wolf and crayfish answer to the same silence.

moonFace.title: The Moon with a Face
moonFace.description: The disc with a countenance, between straight and wavy rays: borrowed, shifting light — lunar truth changes phase according to who looks at it.

dewDrops.title: The Drops of Dew
dewDrops.description: They fall from sky to earth: inspiration and intuition — the dew that is gathered only at dawn, in silence.

dogWolf.title: The Dog and the Wolf
dogWolf.description: The tame and the wild howl at the same Moon: trained nature and untouched nature react to what they cannot control — they reveal themselves in the night.

crayfish.title: The Crayfish
crayfish.description: Emerging from the lake, between the waters and the path: the oldest floor of the unconscious — the primitive, armored fears that rise only when the light dims.

twoTowers.title: The Two Towers
twoTowers.description: The gateway to the unknown: unfinished portals — the passage between the known and the never-mapped; the path runs between them, not around them.

windingPath.title: The Winding Path
windingPath.description: It climbs, turns, vanishes and reappears: the night journey is no straight line — you cross it by trusting whoever drew the trail this way.

theDevil.name: The Devil
theDevil.intro: In the dark grotto the Goat of Mendes presides: the chains hang loose — the prison is optional.

invertedPentagram.title: The Inverted Pentagram
invertedPentagram.description: The five-pointed star turned upside down: spirit facing the ground — matter adored as a god. The symbol is not evil; it merely points the wrong way.

batWings.title: The Bat's Wings
batWings.description: Night wings that never fly upward, only cast shadow: power confined to the underground — the shadow that prefers the cellar to the sky.

torch.title: The Torch
torch.description: The flame in the raised hand descends upon the captives: inverted "illumination" — awareness used to enslave, fire that burns instead of lighting.

chains.title: The Loose Chains
chains.description: Placed within the captives' reach, yet slack: the central revelation of the arcanum — captivity is self-imposed; no one must remain; it is enough to rise and walk out.

captives.title: The Two Captives
captives.description: The naked man and woman, horned and tailed — the very pair of The Lovers, now in shadow: a bond that was communion has become a fetter; desire, possession.

darkCave.title: The Dark Cave
darkCave.description: A setting with no sky and no horizon: the closed world of material worship — there are no stars here because no one looks up.

theSun.name: The Sun
theSun.intro: The reborn child rides at daybreak: nothing to prove, everything to shine.

sunRays.title: The Sun of Straight Rays
sunRays.description: Unlike the Moon, the rays here do not waver — they are spears of light: full consciousness, without distortion or borrowed light — the source is the center itself.

childHorse.title: The Child on the White Horse
childHorse.description: Naked and free on the white mount: the reborn self — innocence recovered after every crossing; the horse is strength purified in the service of joy.

redBanner.title: The Red Banner
redBanner.description: The child holds the banner of victory — yet does not look at it: triumph that needs no display; the red of vitality streaming without war.

sunflowerWall.title: The Wall of Sunflowers
sunflowerWall.description: Four sunflowers turned toward the child — not toward the sun: all nature recognizes what stands higher; when the Sun is within, even flowers turn to it.

redPlume.title: The Red Plume
redPlume.description: The single feather in the child's hair: a touch of will — freedom is not passivity; it demands a point of fire.

judgement.name: Judgement
judgement.intro: The trumpet sounds over the open coffins: to rise again is to remember where you came from.

angelTrumpet.title: The Angel and the Trumpet
angelTrumpet.description: The sound that wakes the dead: the call — no threat, a summons; the same note that is terror to the old structure is dawn to the soul.

flagCross.title: The Banner on the Trumpet
flagCross.description: The flag bearing the cross, fixed to the instrument: the message that descends — the axis between heaven and earth along which resurrection travels.

risenFamily.title: Those Who Rise
risenFamily.description: Man, woman and child rise from the coffins with open arms: memory, welcome and new beginning — the whole self leaving the old form as one leaves an old bed.

coffins.title: The Floating Coffins
coffins.description: On the water, open, they do not sink: the past that served as a cradle becomes a shell — the old form honored for all it allowed, and left behind with gratitude.

seaMountains.title: The Sea and the Mountains
seaMountains.description: In the background, the unconscious (sea) and the journey to come (mountains): awakening is not the end — it is setting out again, now with open eyes.

theWorld.name: The World
theWorld.intro: Inside the laurel wreath, the dancer contains everything: the four living creatures bear witness to the synthesis.

laurelWreath.title: The Laurel Wreath
laurelWreath.description: The living oval that encloses everything: the mandorla of victory and of the womb — the cosmic uterus where all that was lived is completed, and from which everything begins again.

fourCreatures.title: The Four Living Creatures
fourCreatures.description: Angel, eagle, lion and bull in the clouds of the corners: the same as on the Wheel of Fortune, now without books — the Law has become body; what was studied has been embodied.

dancer.title: The Dancer
dancer.description: The soul celebrating the synthesis: nothing to conquer, everything to dance — the center that exists only in motion, holding the opposites in rotation.

twoWands.title: The Two Wands
twoWands.description: One in each hand: the will that no longer divides — evocation and invocation, doing and receiving, both halves of the same dance.

clouds.title: The Clouds in the Corners
clouds.description: The banks of cloud uphold the living creatures: witness that floats — the world seen from above and from within at once; matter rarefied into consciousness.

aceOfWands.name: Ace of Wands
aceOfWands.intro: A hand emerges from a cloud offering a budding wand: the first impulse, the creative spark and the courage to begin. It is fire in its purest state, still formless and full of promise.

handCloud.title: The Hand in the Cloud
handCloud.description: The gift from above: inspiration arrives as a present, not a conquest. The hand offers the wand, but you must take hold of it.

buddingWand.title: The Budding Wand
buddingWand.description: A living staff still sprouting: will is not dead wood but growing force. Each leaf is an idea ready to unfold.

fallingLeaves.title: The Falling Leaves
fallingLeaves.description: Leaves shaped like the Hebrew letter yod (י), first letter of the divine Name, drift in the air: scattered sparks, seeds of possibility carried by the wind.

castleLandscape.title: The Castle and the Landscape
castleLandscape.description: In the distance a castle on a hill and a fertile valley: the destination the first step has not yet reached but can already see.

twoOfWands.name: Two of Wands
twoOfWands.intro: A man on a battlement holds the world in one hand and a wand in the other, gazing at the sea. Planning, choosing a direction and deciding between what he has and what he could win.

globe.title: The Globe in Hand
globe.description: The world fits in the palm of the one who plans: power, reach and responsibility. The sphere reminds him he must still choose where to set it down.

twoWands.title: The Two Wands
twoWands.description: One held, one fixed to the wall: will in motion and will rooted in place. Between what you carry and what you leave standing, strategy is born.

seaHorizon.title: The Sea and the Horizon
seaHorizon.description: His gaze goes past the walls to the open sea: the ambition to leave known territory without yet knowing what lies on the other side.

roseLilyEmblem.title: The Rose and the Lily
roseLilyEmblem.description: Crossed roses and lilies on the wall: desire (rose) and purity (lily) joined in the same decision. A will that chooses with heart and clarity together.

threeOfWands.name: Three of Wands
threeOfWands.intro: Seen from behind, a man on a cliff watches his ships set sail. The first fruits of a plan in motion: wider vision, confident waiting and expansion.

manFromBehind.title: The Man from Behind
manFromBehind.description: He has done his part and now watches: the trust of one who planted the plan and accepts waiting. Facing the horizon, he leaves the past behind.

threeWands.title: The Three Wands
threeWands.description: Three firm staves in the ground: the foundation is already planted. One serves as support for his hand, showing that will can now stand on its own.

shipsSea.title: The Ships at Sea
shipsSea.description: The vessels carry what was invested toward distant lands: work leaving your hands that will someday return with a yield.

goldenSky.title: The Golden Sky
goldenSky.description: An open yellow sky over the sea: the light of optimism, the promise that the chosen path has room to grow.

fourOfWands.name: Four of Wands
fourOfWands.intro: Four wands hold up a garland of flowers over a couple celebrating before the castle. The feast after the effort: stability, home, welcome and community.

garlandCanopy.title: The Garland
garlandCanopy.description: Flowers and fruit hang between the wands like a festive canopy: the fruit of effort has become a shared celebration.

fourWands.title: The Four Wands
fourWands.description: Four raised pillars form a gateway: the four directions, the four elements, a firm base that shelters joy.

celebratingCouple.title: The Celebrating Couple
celebratingCouple.description: Two figures raise bouquets with open arms: shared joy doubles. An achievement is only complete when celebrated in company.

castleGate.title: The Castle and the Bridge
castleGate.description: In the background, the castle with its bridge and the group approaching: home as refuge and meeting place, open to those who arrive.

fiveOfWands.name: Five of Wands
fiveOfWands.intro: Five young men brandish staves in a struggle with no clear winner. Competition, friction and the confused energy of many wills colliding, which can wear down or sharpen those involved.

crossedStaves.title: The Crossed Staves
crossedStaves.description: No blow lands: the staves cross in the air and cancel each other. The contest spends strength without producing a direction.

fiveYouths.title: The Five Youths
fiveYouths.description: No one is a villain: each fights for his place. The card shows the natural friction of people with strong ideas who have not yet learned to cooperate.

mixedClothing.title: The Mismatched Clothes
mixedClothing.description: Each youth wears different colors and styles: no uniform, no team. Diversity, when unorganized, becomes confusion instead of strength.

unevenGround.title: The Uneven Ground
unevenGround.description: Rough ground and an open clearing: a training field, not a war. The conflict here is a test of strength, not a deadly battle.

sixOfWands.name: Six of Wands
sixOfWands.intro: A rider crowned with laurel returns in triumph, surrounded by a crowd of staves. Public victory, recognition and the pride of having won in front of everyone.

laurelWreath.title: The Laurel Wreath
laurelWreath.description: A laurel wreath on the wand and on the rider's head: victory earned and acknowledged in honor. The merit belongs to the one who deserves it.

victoriousRider.title: The Victorious Rider
victoriousRider.description: He rides with head high, red cloak in the wind: the confidence of someone who has won and knows that success brings responsibility.

whiteHorse.title: The White Horse
whiteHorse.description: The white mount, adorned in green: tamed energy and the purity of purpose that led to the conquest, guided by the rider and not the reverse.

crowdOfStaves.title: The Crowd of Staves
crowdOfStaves.description: Followers march on foot around him, raising their staves: personal success depends on the support of many. The glory is shared with those who walked alongside.

sevenOfWands.name: Seven of Wands
sevenOfWands.intro: On a hilltop, a man defends his position against six wands rising from below. Courage, firmness and the decision to hold what is yours even at a disadvantage.

defender.title: The Defender
defender.description: He stands alone on guard, looking down: one who holds a conviction often finds himself like this, at a disadvantage but upright.

sixWandsBelow.title: The Six Wands
sixWandsBelow.description: Six staves rise from below: challenges that give no respite and force a choice about what is worth defending. Pressure reveals what truly matters.

mismatchedShoes.title: The Mismatched Shoes
mismatchedShoes.description: He wears unmatched shoes, as if he had risen in a hurry: defense is not always perfect or prepared, and yet it holds.

highGround.title: The High Ground
highGround.description: The hill gives an advantage to whoever holds it: seeing farther and having ground underfoot. Inner steadiness is the safest terrain there is.

tarotWaite.title: Rider-Waite Tarot
tarotWaite.subtitle: The 78 cards of the Rider-Waite Tarot: 22 major and 56 minor arcana. Tap a card to explore its symbols and correspondences.
tarotWaite.comingSoonText: The interactive regions for this card are still being drawn. Check back soon to explore it symbol by symbol.

minor.majorSubtitle: The 22 cards of the great archetypes, tied to the 22 paths of the Tree of Life.
minor.title: Minor Arcana
minor.subtitle: The 56 cards of everyday life, in four suits that follow the four elements: Wands (fire), Cups (water), Swords (air) and Pentacles (earth).

theFool.name: The Fool
theFool.summary: The Fool is the start of every journey: a leap of faith into the unknown. It stands for pure potential, spontaneity and innocence, yet reminds us that courage without attention can lead to the edge of a cliff.

theMagician.name: The Magician
theMagician.summary: The Magician joins heaven and earth: one hand raised, the other pointing down, channeling will into action. With the four suits on the table, the card shows that skill, focus and communication turn intention into reality.

theHighPriestess.name: The High Priestess
theHighPriestess.summary: Seated between the pillars of the Temple, the High Priestess guards the hidden knowledge behind the veil. She rules intuition, silence and the mysteries of the unconscious, and invites us to listen to what cannot yet be said.

theEmpress.name: The Empress
theEmpress.summary: The Empress is Mother Nature: fertility, beauty and abundance in full bloom. She speaks of creation, pleasure, care and the love that nurtures both ideas and people.

theEmperor.name: The Emperor
theEmperor.summary: The Emperor stands for order, structure and authority. From his stone throne he teaches leadership through discipline and responsibility, and warns against the rigidity of confusing control with strength.

theHierophant.name: The Hierophant
theHierophant.summary: The Hierophant is the teacher of traditions and sacred rites, a bridge between the divine and the community. He symbolizes teaching, institutional faith and inherited values, and asks what deserves to be followed and what should be questioned.

theLovers.name: The Lovers
theLovers.summary: The Lovers speak of union and conscious choice. Beyond romance, the card asks for alignment between heart, values and action, reminding us that every true choice also defines who we are.

theChariot.name: The Chariot
theChariot.summary: The Chariot advances through willpower: the charioteer steers two opposing sphinxes without visible reins. It stands for victory, direction and self-control, the triumph of harmonizing opposing forces toward a goal.

strength.name: Strength
strength.summary: Strength shows a woman calming a lion with gentleness. It is quiet courage, patience and compassionate mastery of instinct, where true power comes from the heart rather than from force.

theHermit.name: The Hermit
theHermit.summary: The Hermit raises his lantern on the mountain and walks alone in search of meaning. He symbolizes introspection, prudence and the wisdom that grows in solitude, lighting the way for those who follow.

wheelOfFortune.name: Wheel of Fortune
wheelOfFortune.summary: The Wheel of Fortune turns the cycles of life: rise, fall and return. It reminds us that nothing is permanent, that fate keeps its own rhythms, and that wisdom lies in adapting to change without losing one's center.

justice.name: Justice
justice.summary: Justice weighs deeds with scales and sword: balance, truth and consequence. She asks for honesty, fair decisions and responsibility, because every cause has its effect.

theHangedMan.name: The Hanged Man
theHangedMan.summary: The Hanged Man hangs upside down, at peace, by his own choice. He stands for surrender, pause and a new perspective: sometimes we only move forward by letting go of control and seeing the world from another angle.

death.name: Death
death.summary: Death rarely speaks of a literal end. It is deep transformation: what must end so that something new can be born. The card asks for courage to release what has completed its cycle and to accept renewal.

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.summary: Temperance pours between two cups in a continuous flow, uniting opposites in harmony. It is the card of inner alchemy: moderation, patience and integration, the middle path that heals and balances.

theDevil.name: The Devil
theDevil.summary: The Devil shows the chains we accept ourselves: attachments, addictions and material illusions. Yet the chains hang loose, and the card invites us to face the shadow in order to reclaim freedom.

theTower.name: The Tower
theTower.summary: The Tower collapses in a flash of lightning: false structures fall all at once. It is the rupture that shakes certainties, painful yet liberating, making room for truth and for rebuilding on firmer ground.

theStar.name: The Star
theStar.summary: The Star appears after the storm, bringing hope, healing and inspiration. A figure pours water onto the land and the pool, a symbol of renewed faith and trust that light guides even through the darkest night.

theMoon.name: The Moon
theMoon.summary: The Moon lights an uncertain path between two towers, where a dog and a wolf howl. It rules dreams, fears and intuition: everything seems unclear, and the card asks us to cross the illusion by trusting instinct.

theSun.name: The Sun
theSun.summary: The Sun shines on a joyful, radiant child: happiness, vitality and clarity. It is the card of honest success, truth in daylight and the energy that gives life to everything it touches.

judgement.name: Judgement
judgement.summary: Judgement is the angel's call that awakens the dead: rebirth, reckoning and absolution. It invites us to heed the inner call, forgive the past and embrace a greater purpose.

theWorld.name: The World
theWorld.summary: The World closes the cycle of the Major Arcana: fulfillment, integration and wholeness. The dancing figure within the wreath celebrates a journey completed, while the next beginning is already taking shape.

aceOfWands.name: Ace of Wands
aceOfWands.summary: A hand emerges from a cloud offering a budding wand: the first impulse, the creative spark and the courage to begin. It is fire in its purest state, still formless and full of promise.

twoOfWands.name: Two of Wands
twoOfWands.summary: A man on a battlement holds the world in one hand and a wand in the other, gazing at the sea. Planning, choosing a direction and deciding between what he has and what he could win.

threeOfWands.name: Three of Wands
threeOfWands.summary: Seen from behind, a man on a cliff watches his ships set sail. The first fruits of a plan in motion: wider vision, confident waiting and expansion.

fourOfWands.name: Four of Wands
fourOfWands.summary: Four wands hold up a garland of flowers over a couple celebrating before the castle. The feast after the effort: stability, home, welcome and community.

fiveOfWands.name: Five of Wands
fiveOfWands.summary: Five young men brandish staves in a struggle with no clear winner. Competition, friction and the confused energy of many wills colliding, which can wear down or sharpen those involved.

sixOfWands.name: Six of Wands
sixOfWands.summary: A rider crowned with laurel returns in triumph, surrounded by a crowd of staves. Public victory, recognition and the pride of having won in front of everyone.

sevenOfWands.name: Seven of Wands
sevenOfWands.summary: On a hilltop, a man defends his position against six wands rising from below. Courage, firmness and the decision to hold what is yours even at a disadvantage.

eightOfWands.name: Eight of Wands
eightOfWands.summary: Eight wands cut across the sky in swift flight toward the ground, with no human figure in sight. Speed, messages and events arriving all at once, with the momentum of something that cannot stop.

nineOfWands.name: Nine of Wands
nineOfWands.summary: Wounded and bandaged, a man leans on his staff before a fence of wands. Weariness, caution and the persistence of someone who has faced much and still has not given up.

tenOfWands.name: Ten of Wands
tenOfWands.summary: Bent under the weight of ten bundled wands, a man walks toward the village in the distance. Overload, too much responsibility taken on, and the need to share the weight.

pageOfWands.name: Page of Wands
pageOfWands.summary: A young man in a tunic patterned with salamanders gazes at the wand he holds, in the middle of the desert. Curiosity, enthusiasm and the message of a new idea asking to be explored.

knightOfWands.name: Knight of Wands
knightOfWands.summary: A knight in armor and a salamander tunic charges on a rearing horse. Drive, adventure and an enthusiasm that does not weigh risk, but can trample whatever is in the way.

queenOfWands.name: Queen of Wands
queenOfWands.summary: Seated on a lion throne with a sunflower in hand and a black cat at her feet, the queen radiates confidence and warmth. Magnetism, generosity and a will that attracts rather than imposes.

kingOfWands.name: King of Wands
kingOfWands.summary: The king in a salamander-patterned mantle holds the budding wand, seated on a lion throne. Vision, charismatic leadership and a mastery of fire that inspires others to follow.

aceOfCups.name: Ace of Cups
aceOfCups.summary: A hand emerges from a cloud offering an overflowing chalice while a dove lowers a wafer onto it. The beginning of a love, an intuition or a grace that pours out without measure.

twoOfCups.name: Two of Cups
twoOfCups.summary: A man and a woman exchange cups beneath the winged caduceus of Hermes. Mutual attraction, partnership and the pact of two who recognize one another in equality and respect.

threeOfCups.name: Three of Cups
threeOfCups.summary: Three women dance with raised cups among fruit and garlands. Shared joy, friendship and the celebration of a harvest nobody won alone.

fourOfCups.name: Four of Cups
fourOfCups.summary: A young man with crossed arms meditates under a tree, ignoring the three cups before him while a hand offers a fourth. Apathy, contemplation and the opportunity that goes unnoticed.

fiveOfCups.name: Five of Cups
fiveOfCups.summary: A cloaked figure in black mourns three spilled cups, without seeing the two still standing behind. Grief, regret and the choice to look at what remains.

sixOfCups.name: Six of Cups
sixOfCups.summary: Two children exchange a cup of flowers in an old village courtyard. Nostalgia, innocence and the sweetness of simple gestures that remind us who we were and what we can still give.

sevenOfCups.name: Seven of Cups
sevenOfCups.summary: Before a dark silhouette, seven cups float among the clouds, each holding a different vision. Fantasy, many options and the need to tell dream from what is possible.

eightOfCups.name: Eight of Cups
eightOfCups.summary: Under an eclipsed moon, a man in a red cloak leaves eight neatly stacked cups behind and climbs toward the mountains. Walking away from what no longer satisfies, in search of deeper meaning.

nineOfCups.name: Nine of Cups
nineOfCups.summary: A satisfied man with crossed arms sits before nine cups arranged in an arc. The wish card: contentment, well-earned pleasure and the joy of being able to enjoy.

tenOfCups.name: Ten of Cups
tenOfCups.summary: Beneath a rainbow of ten cups, a couple raises their arms while two children play before a house. Emotional fulfillment, family harmony and happiness that reaches everyone.

pageOfCups.name: Page of Cups
pageOfCups.summary: A young man in a flowered tunic gazes at a fish emerging from his cup before the sea. An unexpected message, creative sensitivity and an invitation to take imagination seriously.

knightOfCups.name: Knight of Cups
knightOfCups.summary: A knight in winged armor advances calmly, carrying his cup before him. Romance, a sincere offer and the delicacy of one who acts from the heart, in no hurry to conquer.

queenOfCups.name: Queen of Cups
queenOfCups.summary: The queen contemplates an ornate closed cup, seated on a throne by the sea. Deep intuition, compassion and the ability to feel another without losing your own center.

kingOfCups.name: King of Cups
kingOfCups.summary: The king sits on a throne floating on the restless sea, holding cup and sceptre. Mastery of emotion, compassionate wisdom and the calm of one who rules without denying depth.

aceOfSwords.name: Ace of Swords
aceOfSwords.summary: A hand emerges from a cloud gripping a crowned sword flanked by laurel and palm. The moment of clarity: a truth that cuts through confusion and the victory of thought over doubt.

twoOfSwords.name: Two of Swords
twoOfSwords.summary: A blindfolded woman crosses two swords over her chest before a calm sea under a crescent moon. Stalemate, forced balance and a decision postponed for fear of looking.

threeOfSwords.name: Three of Swords
threeOfSwords.summary: A red heart is pierced by three swords under clouds and rain. Grief, betrayal or a truth that hurts: pain that cannot be argued with and must be gone through to heal.

fourOfSwords.name: Four of Swords
fourOfSwords.summary: A knight lies in effigy on a tomb beneath a stained-glass window, with three swords on the wall. A necessary pause, retreat and the rest that restores the mind after a battle.

fiveOfSwords.name: Five of Swords
fiveOfSwords.summary: A man smiles holding three swords while two others walk away defeated. A doubtful victory, conflict won at any cost and the price of winning without generosity.

sixOfSwords.name: Six of Swords
sixOfSwords.summary: A ferryman poles a hooded woman and child across rough water toward calm, with six swords in the hull. Crossing out of crisis: distance, transition and gradual recovery.

sevenOfSwords.name: Seven of Swords
sevenOfSwords.summary: A man tiptoes away carrying five swords and leaves two behind, with a camp in the background. Strategy, stealth and the dilemma between cunning and honesty.

eightOfSwords.name: Eight of Swords
eightOfSwords.summary: A blindfolded, bound woman stands surrounded by eight swords on soaked ground. A sense of imprisonment, fear and the realization that the way out depends on your own perception.

nineOfSwords.name: Nine of Swords
nineOfSwords.summary: Sitting up in bed, a person hides her face in her hands beneath nine swords hung in the dark. Anxiety, guilt and the nights when the mind works against rest.

tenOfSwords.name: Ten of Swords
tenOfSwords.summary: A figure lies face down with ten swords in the back, under a black sky and a dawn on the horizon. The end of a painful cycle: the worst has passed, and something new begins to be born.

pageOfSwords.name: Page of Swords
pageOfSwords.summary: A youth with windblown hair raises a sword on a hill among clouds and birds. Curiosity, vigilance and the agile mind that wants to learn, ask and discover.

knightOfSwords.name: Knight of Swords
knightOfSwords.summary: A knight with raised sword gallops on a white horse as the wind bends the trees. Intellectual drive, quick decisions and a frankness that cuts, sometimes without measuring the impact.

queenOfSwords.name: Queen of Swords
queenOfSwords.summary: The queen with a butterfly crown holds her sword up with one hand and opens the other, on a carved throne. Clarity, independence and the wisdom of one who learned from pain and speaks frankly.

kingOfSwords.name: King of Swords
kingOfSwords.summary: The king with a butterfly crown holds a sword, seated on a throne beneath a cloudy sky. Intellectual authority, justice and the word that governs through logic and ethics.

aceOfPentacles.name: Ace of Pentacles
aceOfPentacles.summary: A hand emerges from a cloud offering a golden pentacle above a flowering garden. A seed of prosperity: a concrete, material and promising opportunity that asks to be planted.

twoOfPentacles.name: Two of Pentacles
twoOfPentacles.summary: A juggler in a tall hat balances two pentacles bound by a figure-eight ribbon amid big waves. Adaptation, flexibility and the art of keeping several fronts going without losing rhythm.

threeOfPentacles.name: Three of Pentacles
threeOfPentacles.summary: In a Gothic hall, a craftsman works on the arch while a monk and a noble discuss the plan. Teamwork, shared mastery and the value of each contribution to a common work.

fourOfPentacles.name: Four of Pentacles
fourOfPentacles.summary: A seated man clutches a pentacle to his chest, has another on his head and two under his feet, before a city. Security, possession and the risk of closing off to protect what you have.

fiveOfPentacles.name: Five of Pentacles
fiveOfPentacles.summary: Two injured beggars walk through snow past an illuminated stained-glass window with five pentacles. Hardship, exclusion and shelter so near yet seemingly out of reach.

sixOfPentacles.name: Six of Pentacles
sixOfPentacles.summary: A merchant in a red robe weighs coins on a scale and gives them to two kneeling beggars. Generosity, reciprocity and the fairness of giving and receiving in the right measure.

sevenOfPentacles.name: Seven of Pentacles
sevenOfPentacles.summary: A young man leans on his hoe and contemplates a bush heavy with seven pentacles. A pause to assess what has been planted, patience and the doubt between waiting and acting.

eightOfPentacles.name: Eight of Pentacles
eightOfPentacles.summary: Seated at a bench, a craftsman carefully engraves each pentacle; several are already finished beside him. Dedication to craft, learning and the pleasure of improving through repetition.

nineOfPentacles.name: Nine of Pentacles
nineOfPentacles.summary: An elegant woman in an embroidered gown walks alone through a vineyard with a falcon on her hand. Independence, earned comfort and the pleasure of enjoying the fruit of your own effort.

tenOfPentacles.name: Ten of Pentacles
tenOfPentacles.summary: Under a stone arch, a patriarch, a couple, a child and two dogs occupy a courtyard where ten pentacles form the Tree of Life. Inheritance, family, tradition and prosperity that spans generations.

pageOfPentacles.name: Page of Pentacles
pageOfPentacles.summary: A young man in a green tunic gazes at a raised pentacle in a plowed field before the mountains. Study, practical curiosity and the start of a project that demands consistency.

knightOfPentacles.name: Knight of Pentacles
knightOfPentacles.summary: An armored knight stays still on a steady black horse, holding a pentacle in a plowed field. Responsibility, perseverance and methodical work that is in no hurry.

queenOfPentacles.name: Queen of Pentacles
queenOfPentacles.summary: The queen on a throne of fruit and goats cradles a pentacle in her lap in a garden with a rabbit. Care, abundance and the practical generosity of one who nurtures her surroundings.

kingOfPentacles.name: King of Pentacles
kingOfPentacles.summary: The king in a mantle of grapes sits on a throne of bulls, holding sceptre and pentacle before his castle. Prosperity, stability and the power of one who built and now administers with generosity.

abyss.name: Veil of the Abyss
abyss.description: Separates the Supernal Triad (the Unknowable Divine) from the rest of the Tree. Crossing it requires the complete dissolution of the ego.

parokhet.name: Veil of Parokhet
parokhet.description: The veil of the Inner Temple. Separates the Higher Self (conscious soul) from the astral world. It is the portal of initiation.

nephesch.name: Veil of Nephesch
nephesch.description: The Rainbow that separates the astral world (unconscious) from the physical world. It is the boundary between dream and matter.

boaz.name: Pillar of Severity
boaz.description: The Pillar of Severity represents the restrictive force, form, discipline, and divine rigor. It is the feminine, passive, and receptive pillar.

jachin.name: Pillar of Mercy
jachin.description: The Pillar of Mercy represents the expansive force, energy, compassion, and divine grace. It is the masculine, active, and projective pillar.

ain.name: Ain
ain.subtitle: Nothing
ain.description: The Absolute Nothing — the primordial state prior to any manifestation. In the Golden Dawn tradition, Ain represents Pure Negativity, the inconceivable Void that precedes even potentiality.
ain.goldenDawn: The first veil of negative existence. Ain is described in Golden Dawn documents as that which completely transcends human comprehension — neither being nor non-being, but the state that precedes both.
ain.principle: Absolute Negativity — beyond existence and non-existence
ain.relation: Precedes Ain Soph — the inconceivable root of the Limitless

ainSoph.name: Ain Soph
ainSoph.subtitle: Limitless
ainSoph.description: The Limitless — infinite expansion without form, measure, or attribute. In the Golden Dawn, Ain Soph represents the second negative abstraction: the infinite potential containing all possibilities but manifesting none.
ainSoph.goldenDawn: The second veil of negative existence. Mathers and Westcott describe Ain Soph as limitless extension — without beginning, end, or direction. It is the concept of pure infinitude before the Light concentrates.
ainSoph.principle: Infinitude without attribute — pure unmanifested potential
ainSoph.relation: Between Ain and Ain Soph Aur — the infinite preceding the Light

ainSophAur.name: Ain Soph Aur
ainSophAur.subtitle: Limitless Light
ainSophAur.description: The Limitless Light — the first irradiation of the Infinite, the primordial creative impulse. In the Golden Dawn, it represents the moment the Absolute decides to emanate: the Light concentrates into a point (Kether) and the Tree of Life is born.
ainSophAur.goldenDawn: The third veil of negative existence. Golden Dawn rituals teach that Ain Soph Aur is the Limitless Light that concentrates into a single point — forming Kether, the Crown. This is the Tzimtzum of Lurianic Kabbalah: the contraction that allows creation.
ainSophAur.principle: Primordial Light — the first impulse of manifestation
ainSophAur.relation: Directly precedes Kether — the source of the first Sephirah

guide.title: Orientation Guide
guide.purpose: The Tree of Life is a tool for personal self-knowledge and inner exploration. It is not a system of moral or religious judgment, nor does it prescribe what is right or wrong. Each sphere and path represents an aspect of human experience that can be recognized, understood, and integrated. Use it as a mirror for reflection, not as a rulebook for behavior.
guide.interpretation: In this application, the Sefirot and the Qliphoth are not presented as opposing forces of good and evil. They represent spectrums of experience — balanced and imbalanced expressions of the same energies. The Qliphoth are understood as shadow aspects, rejected parts of the psyche, or stagnant creative potential waiting to be recognized. This perspective follows the tradition of psychological and transpersonal Kabbalah.
guide.pruning: The word Qliphoth literally means 'shells' or 'husks' — like dead bark on a living tree. The pruning approach involves three steps: recognize the pattern, understand its origin and function, and integrate the energy it contains into conscious life. This is not about eliminating parts of yourself, but about transforming unconscious compulsions into conscious choices.
guide.tips: Explore at your own pace without pressure to understand everything at once. Click on any sphere to see its correspondences and reflect on how they relate to your experience. The search function can help you find specific symbols, archetypes, or correspondences. Remember that personal meaning is more valuable than memorizing traditional attributions.

thaumiel.integration: By recognizing internal duality, one develops the capacity to hold paradoxes without fragmentation, enabling authentic leadership and a unifying vision.
thaumiel.dailyLife: Manifests as a constant need to polarize situations, creating divisions in groups and relationships through rigid 'me against everyone' positioning.

ghogiel.integration: By facing intellectual blockages, one recognizes the difference between accumulated knowledge and lived wisdom, releasing genuine creative flow.
ghogiel.dailyLife: Manifests as creative procrastination, accumulating information without practical application, and a tendency to dismiss one's own ideas before trying them.

satariel.integration: By looking at what one prefers not to see, deep discernment develops along with the ability to distinguish between healthy protection and paralyzing denial.
satariel.dailyLife: Manifests as systematic avoidance of difficult conversations, postponing medical exams, and preferring simplistic explanations for complex situations.

ghagsheblah.integration: By recognizing patterns of conditional generosity, one learns to offer care without attachment to outcomes, cultivating compassion that respects others' autonomy.
ghagsheblah.dailyLife: Manifests as difficulty respecting others' boundaries, offering unsolicited help, and resentment when expected gratitude is not demonstrated.

golohab.integration: By embracing anger as a signal of violated boundaries, destructive energy transforms into assertiveness and the capacity to act with determination in the face of injustice.
golohab.dailyLife: Manifests as disproportionate outbursts of irritation, chronic impatience in traffic or queues, and a tendency to resolve conflicts through intimidation rather than dialogue.

tagimron.integration: By observing the need for recognition, one develops self-esteem based on internal experience rather than external validation, allowing one to shine without overshadowing others.
tagimron.dailyLife: Manifests as excessive seeking of praise, constant comparison with peers on social media, and difficulty celebrating others' achievements without feeling personal diminishment.

gharab.integration: By recognizing desire as a driving force, one learns to channel emotional intensity toward constructive bonds and creative expression rather than compulsive consumption.
gharab.dailyLife: Manifests as impulsive purchases, relationship patterns based on idealization followed by rapid disinterest, and difficulty feeling content with what one already has.

samael.integration: By perceiving one's own rationalization patterns, intellectual honesty and transparent communication develop, using intelligence to clarify rather than obscure.
samael.dailyLife: Manifests as elaborate justifications for contradictory behaviors, use of ambiguous language to avoid commitment, and a tendency to manipulate narratives for personal benefit.

gamaliel.integration: By welcoming instincts without judgment, a conscious relationship with the body and emotional cycles develops, transforming compulsion into directed vitality.
gamaliel.dailyLife: Manifests as oscillations between repression and excessive indulgence, difficulty maintaining regular sleep routines, and using sensory stimulation to avoid contact with underlying emotions.

nahemoth.integration: By recognizing the attraction to material comfort as a need for security, bodily presence develops along with the capacity to inhabit the physical world without getting lost in it.
nahemoth.dailyLife: Manifests as excessive attachment to possessions and routines, difficulty accepting changes in the physical environment, and seeking security exclusively through material accumulation.

daath_qliphoth.integration: By traversing dispersion without resistance, identity rebuilds on broader foundations, integrating previously inaccessible fragments of personal experience.
daath_qliphoth.dailyLife: Manifests as recurring identity crises, a persistent sense of lack of purpose, and difficulty maintaining continuity between projects or life phases.
